newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian peacekeepers told to make peace, not babies.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian peacekeepers told to make peace, not babies.

text.p: The commander of West African peacekeeping troops ECOMOG in Liberia said Nigerian soldiers who married local girls there would be discharged from the army.
"We are here to make peace, not babies," the semi-official Daily Times newspaper on Monday quoted Major-General Sam Victor Malu as saying in the Liberian capital Monrovia.
"You get married to a Liberian, you discharge from the army and leave the barracks a freeman," he told the troops during a tour of ECOMOG operations by Nigerian journalists.
"But if you want to continue to remain in service, get rid of the Liberian woman, marry a Nigerian and remain in the army and we keep you in the barracks."
Nigerians constitute the majority of the 10,000 troops that intervened in 1990 in the Liberian civil war. The war has now ended and election to choose a new president is slated for May.
Daily Times said Nigeria's government was planning a census of hundreds of children fathered by its soldiers in Liberia.
